exposure: Mode of labor induction (breast stimulation, intracervical balloon, spontaneous labor)
Maternal serum levels of oxytocin, prostaglandin F2α, prostaglandin E2, prolactin, estradiol, and cortisol
cohort: 87 women at term with previous cesarean section
finding: Both breast stimulation and intracervical balloon induction resulted in similar induction-to-delivery times and modes of delivery, but hormonal profiles differed between the groups, supporting the hypothesized mechanisms of each induction method.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in mode of delivery between the induction groups, suggesting that neither breast stimulation nor intracervical balloon increased the risk of cesarean delivery.
